niri 26.04 IPC traffic, reconstructed from niri's source at tag v26.04
(the files cited below), not captured from a running niri. Checked
against a real niri 26.04 (niri-26.04-captured, 2026-10-08): the shapes
match; two bursts were reordered to what niri sends (open: the active
window first; close: the focus moves before WindowClosed). This file
keeps the two-output scenario a nested niri cannot show.

niri writes each reply and event as one line of compact JSON
(serde_json::to_writer plus "\n", src/ipc/server.rs at tag v26.04). The
types are niri-ipc/src/lib.rs at v26.04: Reply = Result<Response, String>
serialised externally tagged ({"Ok":…} / {"Err":"…"}); Response::Workspaces,
Response::Windows, Response::FocusedOutput; Event variants as
{"Name":{fields}}; Window with layout and focus_timestamp; Workspace with
idx, name (null when unnamed), output, is_urgent, is_active, is_focused,
active_window_id; Output with modes, logical and transform "Normal".

reply-*.json: the replies to "Workspaces", "Windows" and "FocusedOutput".
events.txt: what the event-stream connection carries. `## stream-start`
is the reply to "EventStream" followed by the state niri replicates to
every new stream (niri-ipc/src/state.rs, EventStreamState::replicate:
workspaces, windows, keyboard layouts, overview, config, casts); the
other `## name` sections are bursts the test sends as one write. Lines
starting with `#` and blank lines are markers, not traffic.

Scenario: DP-1 (focused) with workspaces 1, "chat", 3 and HDMI-A-1 with
workspace 4; Alacritty (focused) on 1, Signal on "chat".
